lessons.title: Supervised vs Unsupervised Learning
lessons.content_md:
# Supervised vs Unsupervised Learning 🎓

How exactly do we feed data into an AI? It turns out there are two main ways an AI can learn: **Supervised Learning** and **Unsupervised Learning**.

## The Teacher Grading Homework (Supervised Learning)

Imagine a student doing math homework with a strict teacher looking over their shoulder. For every problem, the student makes a guess, and the teacher immediately says "Correct" or "Incorrect" because the teacher holds the answer key.

This is **Supervised Learning**.

We give the AI a dataset that is fully **labeled**. For example, 10,000 photos of cats and dogs, where every single photo has a tag attached saying "Cat" or "Dog". The AI makes a guess, checks the label (the answer key), and adjusts its internal math if it was wrong.

<flipcard front="👩‍🏫 What is Supervised Learning?" back="Learning with labeled data. The AI has an 'answer key' and learns by comparing its predictions to the correct answers."></flipcard>

## Organizing a Messy Room (Unsupervised Learning)

Now imagine a child is told to clean a very messy playroom. There are no instructions, no labels, and no teacher. The child has to figure out how to organize things on their own.

They might put all the round things (balls) in one box. They might put all the colorful things (blocks) in another box. They found patterns and grouped things without ever knowing the official names for "balls" or "blocks".

This is **Unsupervised Learning**.

We give the AI a massive pile of **unlabeled** data. It has no answer key. The AI's job is simply to find hidden structures, group similar things together (clustering), or find anomalies.

<flipcard front="🧩 What is Unsupervised Learning?" back="Learning with unlabeled data. The AI looks at raw data without an answer key and tries to find hidden patterns and groupings on its own."></flipcard>

<flipcard front="🛒 Give a real world example of Unsupervised Learning!" back="Netflix recommendations! Netflix groups users with similar watch histories together, even without explicitly labeling them, to suggest new shows."></flipcard>
